outcome: A cost cannot be paid without the full resources for it, such as a tapped permanent that cannot be tapped again or life below the cost.
Paying mana removes it from the mana pool.
Paying life subtracts that amount from the life total.
A spell or ability with an unpayable cost can be attempted, but its cost cannot be paid, so it is not castable or activatable.
An unpayable cost stays unpayable when increased, but an alternative cost such as casting without paying its mana cost makes it payable.
A reduced cost is paid at its reduced amount and counts as paying the original cost.
A generic reduction lowers only the generic component of the cost.
A colored or colorless reduction the cost does not require reduces generic mana instead.
A colored reduction exceeding that color's component removes it and reduces generic mana by the excess.
A colorless reduction exceeding the colorless component removes it and reduces generic mana by the excess.
A reduction by a hybrid symbol reduces the cost by the half the payer chose.
A reduction by a Phyrexian symbol reduces the cost by one mana of its color.
A reduction by snow mana symbols reduces generic mana by that amount.
A spell with a mandatory additional cost involving hidden-zone cards need not be cast by an if-able instruction.
An additional cost leaves the spell's mana cost and mana value unchanged for effects that read it.
Only one alternative cost can apply to a spell as it is cast.
An alternative cost leaves the spell's mana cost and mana value unchanged for effects that read it.
Additional costs, increases and reductions apply on top of the alternative cost being paid.
A single payment, such as a sacrifice, cannot pay costs of two abilities, so the second cannot be paid.
A cost whose paid action was modified by a replacement effect still counts as paid.
An if-you-do clause after a resolution-time cost applies whenever the player chose to pay, even if the action was replaced or could not fully happen.
An unless clause applies its effect only when the player does not pay the unless cost.
An if-you-do clause after an optional search applies whenever the player chose to search, whatever happened afterwards.
Mana may be spent as though it were mana of any type on a cost with that permission.
